subject: how could I compute WAIC with internal variables?

messages.author: 9b1ba46046eac99f
messages.subject: how could I compute WAIC with internal variables?
parts:
Hi Stan,

I am currently working on a simple reinforcement learning model with prediction error value update and softmax action selection.
As I noticed that there are normal_log()-like functions that I could use in the generated quantities section to obtain the log likelihood for WAIC calculation, I am trying to implement it. However, it actually needs the internal value variable that only belongs to the model to calculate the log density. Part of the model is shown below (the full model file is also attached). 

model {
  vector[2] v[nTrials+1];     // values
  for (s in 1:nSubjects) {    
    for (t in 1:nTrials) {
      choice[s,t] ~ categorical_logit( temp[s] * v[t] );
      ...
    }
  }
...
}

In the model, temp is a parameter to be estimated, whereas v is a internal variable. Later in the generated quantities section, I cannot really use something like 
log_lik[s,t] <- categorical_logit_log(choice[s,t],  temp[s] * v[t] );
because v only belongs to the model scope. 

My questions is: is there any possible way to solve this kind of problem? If so, how could I possibly re-construct my model? Indeed, I have another script that could calculate the log likelihood separately using the stanfit output, but I think it is really helpful and convenient to have it in the model file, and calculate it automatically.

Any suggestion or comment is welcome. Thanks in advance.

Best,
Lei

messages.author: 9b1ba46046eac99f
messages.subject: Re: how could I compute WAIC with internal variables?
parts:
Hi Stan,

even I haven't got some feedback yet, I tried something out. In the generated quantities section, I kind of recreate the model again and run over the subject loop and trial loop to generate the log likelihood. The core part of the code is shown below:

generated quantities {
  real log_lik_tw[nSubjects,nTrials]; // trial-wise
  real log_lik[nSubjects]; 
  
  vector[2] v2[nTrials+1];
  vector[nTrials] pe2;
for (s in 1:nSubjects) {
v2[1] <- rep_vector(0.0,2);
for (t in 1:nTrials) {

log_lik_tw[s,t] <- categorical_logit_log(choice[s,t], temp[s] * v2[t]);
     pe2[t]  <- reward[s,t] - v2[t][choice[s,t]];
     v2[t+1] <- v2[t];
     v2[t+1][choice[s,t]] <- v2[t][choice[s,t]] + lr[s] * pe2[t];
   }
   log_lik[s] <- sum( log_lik_tw[s] );
  }
}

But I wasn't sure this is correct way to calculate the log likelihood, because the log likelihood result (and then the WAIC result) is so different than the result I got from using a user-defined R function loglik_RL() as the stanfit object as an input.

I attached the model file, and loglik() function and the WAIC() function, and would like to hear some feedback from anyone.
Thanks a lot in advance!

Best,
Lei

for someone who understood WAIC to answer it.

You can just move the declaration of v to the "transformed parameters"
block.

But what you write for the model block won't work because v isn't
defined at the point where categorical_logit is called.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how could I compute WAIC with internal variables?
parts:
Variables declared in a block may only be assigned in that
block. That means transformed parameters must be fully defined
in the transformed parameters block. There's no information you
don't have at that point, but it may introduce some redundancy.

Stan's not perfect in this regard, which has been commented
on at length by several users on this list, so you may require
some duplicated code (at which point, I'd recommend using a function).

- Bob
